Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

1. Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.330/2022 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Uttam Nagar, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Petitioners No.2 and 3 are not present today as petitioner No.2/mother of petitioner No.1, aged 75 years is unwell and petitioner No.3/sister of petitioner No.1 is looking after their mother.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 does not dispute the identity of petitioners No.2 and 3, hence the petition is taken up disposal.
3. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 28.03.2016 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child was born from this wedlock.
However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other since 05.08.2018.
On the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
During the pendency of proceedings, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 10:34:33 the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 03.12.2022.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Deepak Kumar & Ors vs State (N.C.T. Of Delhi) & Anr on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19610653/
1 Rs.50,000/- to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
4.

entities.text: Deepak Kumar & Ors vs State (N.C.T. Of Delhi) & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.30,000/- to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.501140 dated 02.05.2023 drawn on ICICI Bank for Rs.20,000/- in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

5. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

6. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.330/2022 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Uttam Nagar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
MAY 17, 2023 M
